newsitem.title: UK: Mastercard takes majority stake in Mondex card.
newsitem.headline: Mastercard takes majority stake in Mondex card.

text.p: Payments company MasterCard International said Monday it will acquire a 51 percent stake in London-based Mondex International, a new payment smart card or electronic purse.

Prepaid smart cards, which resemble debit cards, are embedded computer chips that allow consumers to store value and keep track of small purchases. The cards have begun to replace cash at public telephones, vending machines, subways and laundromats.
Mondex Chief Executive Michael Keegan said the deal would speed the introduction of Mondex which is now running pilot schemes in Britain, Hong Kong, Canada, New Zealand and the United States.
"Today's news means that Mondex will be in more pockets and purses, in more countries, more quickly than we had previously planned," Keegan said.
No financial details were released but, when it was set up in July, Mondex International was capitalised at 100 million pounds ($167 million).

Mondex is owned by its 17 "Global Founders" who include National Westminster Bank; Midland Bank and HongKong & Shanghai Banking Corp., both units of HSBC Holdings; AT&T Corp.; Wells Fargo; Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce and ANZ.
MasterCard has around 23,000 members globally who have issued some 370 million credit and debit cards.

Mondex said the stored value card, or electronic purse, is only the first application of the Mondex operating system. It said future technology will support integrated multi-function cards and proprietary cards for such things as loyalty programmes and data transfer.

Currently, the Mondex card can download "money" from the cardholders bank account and be used in shops to make purchases in the normal way. Cardholders can keep track of how much "cash" is held in their card.

Mondex says the average transaction amount in its British pilot has been 6.50 pounds ($10.84) and the average withdrawal 25 pounds ($41.71). Figures from other pilots in Hong Kong and elsewhere have produced similar results.
